messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: autoscaler alert — GPU pool 'shared-nvidia' >= 95% utilization for 7m; queue growth detected (inference-queue length = 12k). Potential autoscale failures and pod backpressure. Paging on-call.

tess-oncall: on it. seeing throttling spikes in the gateway metrics. routing errors (503) up ~18% on prod region-us-west-2. tagging SRE. @jamal-sre can you join?

jamal-sre: joining. grabbing logs for the autoscaler controller. quick check: `kubectl -n infra logs deploy/autoscaler-controller --since=15m`

jamal-sre: output shows repeated scale attempts failing due to insufficient allocatable GPUs: "requested 8, allocatable 6" across nodes. looks like binpacking+MIG fragmentation.

raj-allocator: I see many nodes with unused fractional MIGs — a lot of 1g slices and some 4g, but pods request full GPUs (or 8g equivalents) so scheduler can't place. this causes stranded capacity.

mike-ml: can you paste the `nvidia-smi`/MIG breakdown? curious if recent model rollout changed preferred GPU size.

jamal-sre: pasted snippet from node-exporter (summarized):
```
node-42: 2xA100-MIG(4g), 3xA100-MIG(1g) => free 3*1g but not enough to satisfy 4g requests
node-43: 1xA100-MIG(4g) free, lots of 1g fragments
node-44: 0 free full GPUs, 5x1g free scattered
```

tess-oncall: that matches packet of failed scheduling events `FailedScheduling: 0/25 nodes are available: 14 Insufficient gpu, 11 NodeAffinity.` Looks like autoscaler tried to add nodes but hit cluster quota/ASG limits.

jamal-sre: autoscaler logs show scale-up request created but AWS ASG rejected due to `max-size` reached for that group. and because pods are large we have queue backlog.

sara-cs: i'm seeing customers reporting higher latency in the dashboard — a few high-priority customers in private deployments were impacted. ticket volume rising.

tess-oncall: priority order: 1) mitigate customer impact (evict low-priority jobs / re-route high-priority), 2) unblock scheduler (temporary packing change), 3) root cause (MIG mix + ASG limits).

raj-allocator: mitigation idea: temporarily allow scheduler to pack multiple smaller MIGs into composite allocation by enabling multi-MIG binpack feature — but that requires kernel-level changes. risky. alternative: change admission-controller to allow low-priority workloads to be preempted.

jamal-sre: faster: create emergency override nodepool with homogeneous full-GPU nodes (no MIGs) — spin up n4ds (or dedicated A100 nodes) in a new ASG with higher max-size. need approval to bump infra quota.

tess-oncall: can we do a smaller blast radius? create a new nodepool `ephemeral-fullgpu` with 6 nodes, taint them `gpureserve=true:NoSchedule`, and drain low-priority pods onto it.

raj-allocator: I can open ASG increase request but it may take 5–10m. meanwhile we can throttle low-priority routing at the API gateway. mike-ml, can you flip routing for non-prod / low-prio?

mike-ml: yes, I can set `x-redwood-priority` header override for batch jobs to `low` so the gateway rejects or delays them. applying now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: patch `gateway/priority-filter` at sha abc123 -> applying to prod-us-west-2

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded in 3m 12s — new rule rejecting priority < medium for inference route.

tess-oncall: immediate effect: inflow to the queue dropped ~40% and request rate stabilized. queue length down to 7.2k. good.

jamal-sre: ASG increase approved by infra (requested +6 nodes). provisioning new `ephemeral-fullgpu` pool.

raj-allocator: while nodes come up, we should also reclaim fragmented capacity by doing selective MIG reconfiguration on a few nodes: convert mixed 1g+4g into 1x8g equivalent (disable MIG slices) on 3 nodes and mark scheduling-pool. note: this causes pods to be evicted and restarted — coordinate with oncall.

tess-oncall: agree, but only do on nodes with mostly low-priority batch pods. jamal, coordinate with node drains. i'll message ops to expect evictions.

jamal-sre: starting node drain on node-44 -> cordon -> drain low-prio pod set. command: 
```
kubectl cordon node-44
kubectl drain node-44 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app in (batch, training)'
```

jamal-sre: node drained. performing MIG reconfigure (out-of-band) — will take ~90s for driver restart.

jamal-sre: MIG reconfig successful on node-44. it now exposes 1 full-GPU allocation instead of 5x1g. adding node back to cluster.

tess-oncall: good. scheduler accepted 2 pending large pods on node-44. queue dropped further to 3.5k. some latency-sensitive calls still throttled but reduced.

sara-cs: passing updates to customers: "We've applied a temporary mitigation to reduce latency and are provisioning additional full-GPU capacity. Some batch jobs may be delayed."

mike-ml: note — the recent model rollout changed the recommended GPU request from 4g -> 8g for new containers. we should have updated nodepool labels / quotas. action item.

raj-allocator: ASG `ephemeral-fullgpu` is now healthy with 6 nodes. autoscaler registered them. pending pods draining into new pool.

jamal-sre: final queue steady-state at 600 requests, error rate back to baseline. throttling resolved.

tess-oncall: handing off to @raj-allocator for post-incident follow-up and capacity planning. oncall -> @raj-allocator at 2026-03-14T18:23:19Z.

raj-allocator: taking postmortem. preliminary RCA: mixed MIG sizes + new workloads requesting larger GPU footprints + ASG max-size limits prevented autoscaler from adding sufficient resources, leading to scheduler rejections and queue growth. stranded capacity caused by fragmentation.

raj-allocator: action items (short): [1] standardize MIG profiles in nodepool templates; [2] add ASG headroom alert when cluster has >85% gpu and ASG at max-size; [3] add admission-controller preemption for low-priority jobs; [4] update deployment docs for new model GPU footprints.

sara-cs: filing customer postmortem note and escalation for impacted customers.

tess-oncall: closing incident channel for now. will create incident ticket INC-2026-0314-01 and assign to raj-allocator for follow-up. thanks everyone. :tada:
